# Birding journal

Day 1. Out at the oak wood behind the farm at dawn with low mist that burned off by nine. I counted 3 stonechats and watched a hunting hobby for most of an hour from the hide. Through the scope the plumage details were clear: worn wing coverts, fresh tail feathers, and a faint buff wash on the breast that the field guide does not mention. Noted the calls in the log and moved on.

Through the scope the plumage details were clear: worn wing coverts, fresh tail feathers, and a faint buff wash on the breast that the field guide does not mention. Noted the calls in the log and moved on.

On the last night the sleeping mat went flat again. The fix that finally held: inflate it fully, brush soapy water over the surface until a stream of tiny bubbles shows the hole, dry the spot, rough it up with the sandpaper from the repair kit, and press a patch on with the glue for a full minute.

Leave the patched mat inflated overnight before trusting it again, and keep the spare patches and the small tube of glue in the lid pocket of the rucksack so they are at hand next time it slowly deflates under me at 3 am.
